evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (CUHK Multi-function Chinese Character Database)
evidence.text: Analyzes 您 as 心 (semantic) plus 你 (sound), used as a second-person pronoun. It cites a Jin-period passage from 董解元《西廂記諸宮調》卷五 and a Yuan-period example from 白樸《梧桐雨》 where 您 addresses a group. The source supports the component analysis and these cited uses; it does not provide a dated manuscript witness or a sequence of earlier graph forms.
evidence.kind: character-specific dictionary analysis and quoted attestations
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「您」

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: States 您 is not recorded in 說文. Defines it as an honorific second-person pronoun, also used broadly for plural ‘you’, and cites examples from 五代史平話 and Yuan 張國賓《合汗衫》. Its entry is lexicographic evidence for those cited uses, not an explanation of the graph's formation.
evidence.title: [A01365] 您 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: 賈若琛, “『您』来了：『您』作为现代汉语普通话第二人称敬称成因新释” (ResearchGate-hosted thesis text)
evidence.field: corpus search; earlier proposals; historical use
evidence.text: The author reports that searches of CCL, BCC, and Academia Sinica corpora found 您 as a pronoun from Yuan onward, while a Tang/Five Dynasties epitaph instance “并州您管” was judged a likely textual error and not a pronoun. The text reviews competing derivations: contraction of 你們/你每, contraction of 你老 or 你老人家, nasalization/contact proposals, and a possible relation between plural and honorific use. It also presents disagreement about whether the modern honorific descends from the earlier plural pronoun and when the honorific use arose. These are the thesis author's review and corpus-search claims, not independent verification of the corpora or epitaph witness.
evidence.kind: secondary scholarly review and corpus-search report
evidence.title: “您”来了：“您”作为现代汉语普通话第二人称敬称成因新释

evidence.text: For 你, the database describes a second-person singular pronoun absent from oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions and 說文, and cites 《集韻·止韻》 and 《隋書·李密傳》. Its current Mandarin display is incomplete in the captured page, so this page is not used to assert a specific modern reading or an ancient sound match with 您.

evidence.text: The dictionary records a handwritten form under 您, citing 元曲選《漢宮秋》, and says its standard printed form is 恁. This establishes a documented written-form relation in that cited dictionary record; it does not establish the original formation or pronunciation of 您.

search_audit.query: official Unicode Unihan page for 您 U+60A8 and 你 U+4F60; open Unicode FAQ and Xiaoxuetang rights notice
search_audit.outcome: Both official character-specific Unihan pages returned internal errors in the browser. The Unicode FAQ opened and was inspected. Xiaoxuetang rights notice opened without useful extractable page text; the supplied per-character query says 您 was unavailable with HTTP 401.

gaps: The exact earliest surviving graphic form of 您, the date and witness for the first use of the compound graph, and any intervening graphic changes remain unestablished. MOE says 您 is absent from 說文; the sources inspected do not supply a sequence of earlier glyphs.

The CUHK Jin/Yuan quotations and MOE's Five Dynasties/Yuan examples are dictionary-reported attestations; the manuscript or edition witnesses were not independently inspected. The thesis reports Yuan as the earliest corpus period and judges the Tang/Five Dynasties epitaph instance a likely corruption/non-pronoun, but the underlying epitaph versions and corpus records were not checked.

The early spoken word's origin remains unsettled. Proposed sources include contraction of 你們/你每, contraction of 你老/你老人家, nasalization or contact accounts, and possible relation to Buddhist 仁. The sources inspected do not independently demonstrate the required source-word pronunciations and sound changes for any one derivation.
The relationship between early singular/plural 您/恁 use and modern honorific use is disputed; the inspected sources do not settle the semantic path or securely date the honorific extension.

The source analysis supports 你 as the sound component and 心 as semantic, but the exact historical pronunciation match at the time 您 was formed was not verified. The local supplied Unihan rows give current kMandarin 你 nǐ and 您 nín; these are modern readings and do not establish ancient phonetic correspondence. Official character-specific Unicode links were attempted but inaccessible, so no external official click-through evidence for those rows is included.
The supplied Baxter–Sagart table rows cover only 丙, not 您 or 你. No local historical reconstructions for either character were available to cross-check; no reconstruction is asserted.

No historical image candidate was selected. The one inspected Commons glyph is a modern seal-style computer reconstruction of 你 rather than a historical artifact, and its exact image URL was already unavailable after a 404. The Xiaoxuetang query for 您 returned HTTP 401 with no candidates; no usable alternate source with direct-image identity and reuse rights was verified.

limitations.text: No usable historical glyph image of 您, or relevant reusable historical form image, was established in this search. The Commons candidate depicts a modern computer reconstruction of 你 in a seal-style font rather than an ancient artifact, and its previously attempted exact image URL returned 404. The official Xiaoxuetang query supplied for 您 returned HTTP 401 with no candidates. MOE lists historical dictionary witnesses but its page does not establish a direct reusable image asset or reuse permission.
